newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: BellSouth's Telcel eyes Venezuela basic phone mkt.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth's Telcel eyes Venezuela basic phone mkt.

text.p: BellSouth's Venezuelan cellular telephone unit Telcel is positioning itself to compete in basic telephone services once national phone company CANTV's monopoly expires, a top Telcel official said.
Telcel is currently working to install a network of 400 signal boosters nationwide, Telcel President Oswaldo Cisneros said.
"This means that we are going to be able to compete in basic phone services in every area of the country," Cisneros said.
The monopoly of GTE Corp- run CANTV will run out in November 2000.
"The big question is how this opening up is managed, whether it will be through auctions or joint ventures," Cisneros said.
Telcel currently has 463,000 customers, or 55 percent of the cellular telephone market, Cisneros said.
CANTV's Movilnet controls the remainder of the market -- Latin America's densest at 35 cellular phone lines per 1,000 inhabitants.
Cisneros, president of the Grupo Cisneros which holds the Telcel joint venture with BellSouth, criticized CANTV for levying a charge for accessing its network.
"Instead of paying a call at 12 bolivars ($0.02) we pay 22 bolivars ($0.04) every time we communicate with the CANTV network," he said.
Cisneros labeled the charge a "subsidy" which had been established when the company was first privatized in 1991 but should now be dropped.
"We are talking to them, company to company, and trying to reach an agreement," he said.
